reason: The code is a single Linear(window=128 -> 1) plus bias over 262k rows. As a linear with only a bias add it falls under 8p, but out_features=1 makes it a bandwidth-bound GEMV (a dot product per row), which needs a different kernel from 8p's compute-bound 8192x8192x28672 GEMM. The rubric's 'differs only in shape' rule and the 'judge by kernel design' rule point in opposite directions here.

Attention pooling where score = x @ a (one learned query), softmax over the sequence, then a weighted sum of x. That is softmax(qK^T)V with Lq=1 and K=V=x, the plain SDPA algorithm at a decode-like shape with no scale.

DANet channel attention: energy = X X^T, softmax(rowmax - energy), which equals softmax(-X X^T), then multiplied by X. This is softmax(QK^T)V with Q=K=V and a negation score mod, which the rubric's correction excludes. Only the geometry differs (256 channel tokens, head dim 16384).

There are two single-head attention layers, each softmax((q@k)*mask - penalty*(1-mask))@v, which is SDPA with a dense elementwise score mod (1p/5p algorithm). They sit between ReLU linear projections, an encoder linear and a head. SDPA is about 30% of FLOPs; the rest is 10 Gemm+bias+ReLU layers, so it is mostly an attention-layer stack but not SDPA-dominated.

The whole computation is one GEMM (x @ w, no bias) followed by LeakyReLU(0.2). That is 20k's Gemm->Multiply->LeakyReLU chain (equivalently 8p plus one activation), differing only in the bias, the constant scale and the slope.
About 99.8% of FLOPs are a 131072x512x512 GEMM with bias and ReLU, which is exactly 41k's op chain. What follows is a tiny 512->1 GEMV plus sigmoid, which counts as trivial post-processing.

Two set-attention blocks, each with bias linear projections around plain non-causal multi-head SDPA (256 inducing points against 4096 elements, head dim 128). Attention is about 47% of FLOPs and is the only non-GEMM kernel; the rest is plain bias GEMMs (8p) and residual/ReLU epilogues, so no part falls outside JAXBench's algorithms.

These are two Set Transformer MAB blocks, each linear q/k/v, then plain non-causal multi-head softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V cross-attention between 128 inducing points and 4096 points, then a residual ReLU linear. The only non-GEMM kernel is 1p's SDPA, but it is about 20% of FLOPs next to the bias-only projections, so it is an attention-layer stack rather than an SDPA-dominated problem.

Core is log_softmax over the class axis, dotted with label-smoothed one-hot targets, with ignore-index masking and a mean: softmax CE whose only change is label smoothing. The rubric names that case borderline. It also lacks 13p's dominant fused lm-head matmul.

A two-layer MLP with two 8192x2048x2048 f32 GEMMs: the first is GEMM + bias + ReLU (41k's exact chain) and the second is GEMM + bias (8p). It is the 9p MLP pattern without the gate, so every part is a JAXBench algorithm.

This is a three-layer MLP; over 99% of its FLOPs are two Gemm+bias+ReLU layers, which is exactly 41k's op chain at different shapes. The final 512->1 matvec plus sigmoid is trivial post-processing, and there is no gating despite the glu flag.

After the no-op axis swap it is LayerNorm, then Linear + GELU, then Linear over D=512. FLOPs are dominated by two 131072x512x512 bias GEMMs (8p/9p-style MLP). I could not decide whether the fused LayerNorm prologue (centred, a non-JAXBench op) is substantial enough to keep it.

Q/K/V linear projections, then multi-head softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d) + dense additive mask)V, then an output projection. Attention dominates the FLOPs, and SDPA with an arbitrary additive score bias is 5p's algorithm (1p without the bias).

A standard MHA module: Q/K/V projections, scaled softmax(QK^T)V (non-causal, one head of dim 1024), and an output projection. The core is plain SDPA, and the projections around it are plain GEMMs (8p).

Most of the FLOPs (about 80%) are a 4096x4096 theta@phi score matrix, a softmax and @g, wrapped in 1x1 convs and a residual. The softmax is over axis=1, the query axis, not the keys. The structure and cost are 1p's, but the column normalisation rules out flash-style online softmax over keys and needs a two-pass, attention-backward-like design.

A 1x1 conv and theta/phi/g projections, then single-head non-causal softmax(theta phi^T/sqrt(d)) g (about 44% of FLOPs), then an output linear and a residual. Its core is plain SDPA wrapped in GEMMs; the extra 1/sqrt(n) scale and residual are trivial.

Set attention block: Q/K/V projections, multi-head non-causal softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V, a residual on Q, then o + ReLU(Linear(o)). It is plain SDPA plus plain GEMMs, with no norms or multi-layer FFN that would make it a larger block.

A set-attention block: QKV bias projections, plain non-causal 4-head SDPA (N=2048, head dim 256), an output projection with residual, and a ReLU linear residual. Attention is about 45% of FLOPs and the only non-GEMM kernel; the rest is bias GEMMs and GEMM+ReLU (8p/41k), so nothing is materially different from JAXBench tasks.

After mean-variance norm and 1x1-conv projections, the core is S = softmax(F^T G) over the key axis, then O = H S^T. That is plain non-causal single-head softmax(QK^T)V with seq 4096 and head dim 1024. The SDPA is about 2/3 of FLOPs; the projections, norm and output conv are surrounding processing.
Fused QKV projection, then multi-head scaled dot-product softmax(QK^T)V (non-causal here), then an output projection. This is standard MHA SDPA, the same algorithm as 1p apart from the causal mask.

Only matmuls: two bias projections (about 80% of FLOPs) and a batched Q @ K^T divided by sqrt(d), with no softmax and no V. Every step is a plain matmul with at most a bias add or a scale, which is 8p's algorithm.

There are four set encoders, each two Gemm+bias+ReLU layers (41k's chain, dominant in FLOPs), followed by a masked mean pool over the set axis, a concat, and a small ReLU/sigmoid head. The float masks are as large as the hidden activations, so the masked pooling dominates bytes and changes the fused-kernel design: it is a reduction over M, not a GEMM epilogue.

NLL over log-probabilities with integer targets: take_along_axis gather of the target log-prob, then a sequence-mask-weighted mean over time. The rubric lists NLL with integer targets under 13p. The extra masking is trivial post-processing, though the gather is only the target-pick step of 13p's CE.

This is flatten, then two Linear+bias+ReLU layers. The first, a 2048x8192 @ 8192x2048 GEMM, is about 80% of FLOPs and is exactly 41k's Gemm->Add->ReLU chain at different shapes. The second layer is the same algorithm again, and there is no gating despite the glu flag.

Packed QKV projection, then multi-head non-causal cross-attention softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V (L=1024, S=2048), then an output linear and an elementwise multiply with tgt. Attention is the largest FLOP term and is plain SDPA.

This is Bahdanau additive attention: a GEMM with bias and tanh, a dot with a learned query vector, a softmax over candidates, then a weighted sum. Most of the FLOPs are in the GEMM, tanh and matvec score path, and there is no QK^T. The rubric keeps MLP-score attention, and the op chain does not match any k-task.

Weight-normed Linear+ReLU projections of v and q, then a per-channel bilinear pooling v^T A q over a given attention map, then a final linear (BAN-style). There is no softmax(QK^T)V, and the bilinear contraction does not match any JAXBench algorithm.

An elementwise class-balanced binary log loss with beta**(p**gamma) focal-style weights and a global mean. There is no softmax over classes and no integer-target gather, so it is different math from 13p's softmax cross-entropy.

This is an additive (Bahdanau) score: tanh(x@Wx + broadcast(s@Ws)) @ w, then a softmax over T, and it returns only the weights. The large x projection dominates, followed by an activation and a reduction over N. That is MLP-score attention with no QK^T and no V, and the chain is not a k-task's.

Bahdanau additive attention scores: tanh(W_x x + W_s s) projected to a scalar, then softmax over time, returning only the weights. The rubric lists additive MLP-score attention as keep, and there is no QK^T or V product.

Row-wise cosine similarity between 2048 rows of width 16384 (three row reductions, dominated by bytes), then a 2048x2048 GEMV with bias and a softmax over one 1-D vector. It is not softmax(QK^T)V and matches no JAXBench algorithm.

This is additive tanh attention (Show-Attend-Tell style) with odd broadcasting. att1 + att2[:,None] grows to (8,8,128,128,128), the softmax runs over the size-8 axis, and alpha*att1 grows to about 1e9 elements before the sum. The cost is memory- and VPU-bound broadcast arithmetic, with no softmax(QK^T)V.

Show-Attend-Tell additive attention: ReLU(W_e enc + W_d dec), scalar score, softmax over pixels, weighted sum of encoder features. This is MLP-score (Bahdanau) attention, which the rubric keeps; it is not softmax(QK^T)V.

A global average pool over a large NCHW tensor dominates. It feeds a tiny two-layer MLP and a hard Gumbel-softmax over 2 outputs, which is an SE-style gate, not attention. 39k shares only the pooling step, and its core is a conv.
Attentive pooling: Linear-ReLU-Linear scalar score, plus an additive mask, softmax, weighted sum. The scores come from an MLP, not a QK^T product, so this is additive attention pooling (keep).

Bahdanau additive attention: linear(enc) + linear(dec), then tanh, a linear score to 1, and log_softmax over the source sequence. The score is an additive MLP and there is no QK^T and no V aggregation, which the rubric lists as a keep.

This is an elementwise binary cross-entropy with logits (log_sigmoid) against one-hot targets after a constant logit shift, then a mean. There is no softmax or log-sum-exp normalisation over classes and no fused matmul, so the math differs from 13p's softmax CE.
Elementwise LSQ-style fake quantization: divide by step, round (STE), clip, rescale. A purely elementwise op, unrelated to the quantized attention in 65p or any other JAXBench task.

This is a soft-target distillation loss, sum(-softmax(t/T) * log_softmax(s/T)), over a non-last class axis, with no integer labels and no matmul. The rubric keeps KL-style losses as different math from plain CE, and 13p's core is the fused linear plus CE.

CBAM-style channel attention with group-equivariant rolled weights: mean/max spatial pooling, a two-layer contraction, then a sigmoid gate. Sigmoid channel gates are listed as keep and are not softmax(QK^T)V.

Additive attention: linear(enc) and linear(dec) are concatenated, then ReLU, a linear score to 1, softmax over pixels, and a weighted sum of the encoder output. The score comes from an MLP rather than a QK^T dot product (Bahdanau family), which the rubric lists as a keep.
Soft Dice loss: sums of p*t, p^2 and t^2 over spatial axes, then a Dice ratio and a mean. The rubric names dice loss as different math from cross-entropy (keep).
Soft Dice loss: elementwise product and sums over the spatial axes, a smoothed ratio, then a mean. The rubric lists Dice loss as different math from cross-entropy.

This is a dice loss: sigmoid, then global sums for intersection and union, then 1 - dice. It is a memory-bound elementwise reduction, and the rubric explicitly lists dice loss as different math from CE.
Sigmoid followed by a global Dice ratio (2*sum(p*t)/(sum p + sum t)). Dice loss is a keep under the rubric, and there is no softmax or log-likelihood over classes.
Sigmoid then global Dice: sums of p*t, p and t, then 1 - 2I/U. These are bandwidth-bound global reductions, and Dice loss is an explicit keep in the rubric.

This is a full pre-LN transformer encoder block: LayerNorm, QKV projections, 4-head non-causal SDPA, output projection, residual, LayerNorm, a GELU FFN, and residual. SDPA is only about 14% of FLOPs next to the projections, FFN and LayerNorms, which matches the rubric's keep example of a transformer block.

A global average pool over an 8x128x256x256 tensor dominates; it is a memory-bound reduction, followed by a tiny 8x128 @ 128x512 linear. Pooling is not in JAXBench, and the linear is negligible, so it is not 8p.

The work is a bandwidth-bound global average pool over a large NCHW tensor, followed by a tiny 128->8 linear and a tanh. No JAXBench task has this algorithm: 39k is dominated by its conv, and there is no attention.
Evidential (Dirichlet) KL regularizer built from lgamma/digamma terms over class sums. The rubric lists KL losses as keep, and this is not softmax cross-entropy.
Additive attention scoring: tanh(W_k k + W_q q), then a linear score, softmax over time, and a weighted sum of v. Bahdanau-style MLP scores are not QK^T, which the rubric lists as a keep.

This is an LSTM cell step: four parallel GEMMs on concat(x,h), a sigmoid/tanh gate epilogue, and the cell and hidden state update. It resembles 9p's fused gate/up GEMMs, but there is no down projection and the gating includes a recurrent cell state, so it is a distinct algorithm, not SwiGLU or a k-task chain.
Concat(user, item, metapath), then Linear-ReLU-Linear-ReLU scalar scores, softmax over metapaths and a weighted sum. This is additive MLP-score attention pooling (keep), not a QK^T product.

This is MobileViTv2 separable linear attention: a per-token scalar score, a softmax over tokens, a weighted sum of key projections into one context vector, multiplication into the value projection, and an output linear. There is no QK^T score matrix, so it is linear-complexity attention, not softmax(QK^T)V.

Prototypical-network loss. FLOPs are dominated by a broadcast pairwise squared-distance (128^4 elements), followed by log_softmax over a 128-wide axis, a soft-label weighted mean against dense float labels, and argmax accuracy. 13p instead fuses a vocab-scale linear with integer-target CE.

There is no attention here: a max-pool pyramid (1/2/4) with two 512-channel 2D transposed convolutions upsampling the coarse branches, then summed. Transposed convolution dominates; that is a conv workload, and 28k only shares the conv-transpose primitive (3D, with LN and GELU).
A 1x1 conv down to one channel, a sigmoid, then an elementwise multiply with the input. This is a spatial sigmoid gate (CBAM-like), not softmax attention, and matches no JAXBench op chain.

Bilinear grid_sample gathers over an avg-pool pyramid, a channel concat, and a feature-weighted sum plus bias. This is gather and interpolation work with no attention or JAXBench counterpart; the 'attention' flag is wrong.

This is ASTGCN spatial attention: bilinear reductions of x, an (n,n) product, a bias and sigmoid, Vs @ (.), and a softmax over axis 1 (the matmul's row axis). There is no V aggregation and no softmax(QK^T)V. The softmax sits on a different axis and after a sigmoid gate, so it is not 38k's chain either.

Elementwise numerically stable binary cross-entropy with logits, relu(x) - x*z + log1p(exp(-|x|)), then sum and mean. It is bandwidth-bound sigmoid-BCE with no softmax over classes, so the math differs from 13p.

This is a batched chain of small matmuls: memory @ (W @ topic_emb.T), where the 4D .T reverses the batch axes, then a softmax over axis 2 (the 128 sequence/query axis, not the 64 topics), then @ topic_emb. The Luong-general bilinear score, softmax over queries and tiny VMEM-resident per-item matrices do not make it flash/SDPA.

Full post-LN transformer encoder block: padding-masked MHA, residual + LayerNorm, ReLU FFN (d->2d->d), residual + LayerNorm. The SDPA is about 11% of FLOPs, with the FFN and projections dominating. The rubric keeps a transformer block where attention is one of several substantial parts, and centred LayerNorm is not RMSNorm.

An L1 triplet margin loss (three of the five input tensors, about 60% of bytes) plus a soft-target CE: log_softmax over the 128-wide channel axis of NCHW, dotted with dense labels. The CE part is a non-minor-axis soft-label variant with no linear and no vocab tiling, and the triplet part is unrelated to any JAXBench task.

Scores come from a learned vector (no QK^T). They are masked, broadcast to (8,8,128,128,128), and the softmax runs over a size-8 broadcast axis that is not the one contracted in the following batched matmul with x^T. Because the dominant cost is a broadcast batched matmul whose softmax axis is not the contracted axis, it is not softmax(QK^T)V.

A mean-pooled init state feeds an MLP-score attention (concat, Linear(2d->1), ReLU), a softmax over time, a weighted sum of encoder states, and small Linear+ReLU/Linear heads. It is additive-style attention with no QK^T, and the cost is memory-bound passes over the encoder tensor.
Squeeze-excitation block: global average pool, Linear-ReLU-Linear-Sigmoid, channel-wise rescale of the input. An SE sigmoid gate is explicitly a keep and is not softmax(QK^T)V.

Gumbel-softmax sampler: double-log noise transform, a tempered row softmax over 2048 classes, then a hard one-hot via max/argmax with a straight-through estimator. There is no matmul and no CE loss, so it matches no JAXBench task.

This is a softmax over the batch axis (size 8), then clamped binary cross-entropy terms t*log p + (1-t)*log(1-p) against soft targets, summed over channels and averaged. It is BCE on soft targets with an unusual normalisation axis, not integer-target softmax CE.
